title: CytoWave: Perturbation-Centric Pretraining for Single-Cell Response Prediction
claim: A two-stage pretraining pipeline first learns control-state representations, then learns a perturbation operator with reconstruction and contrastive alignment objectives.
layout: 2 stacked stage panels, left-to-right flow, dashed loss paths, vertical encoder/decoder pills
description: A dense architecture diagram split into two rounded gray panels labeled Stage 1 (top) and Stage 2 (bottom, larger). Inputs on the left are control and perturbed cells, shown as lists of Gene/Expr/Meta tokens. These pass through FiLM into small colored heatmap-strip embeddings (blue for gene, green for meta, pink for cell). Embeddings are concatenated and fed into a tall pink vertical pill, the Joint Transformer Encoder. Stage 1 sends the control embedding plus a query gene embedding to a Query-based Decoder, which outputs the predicted control expression. Stage 2 adds a Perturbation Operator, an Alignment Head and pooling of perturbation embeddings. Dashed lines return the MSE and InfoNCE losses. Math notation labels every tensor. The eye goes first to the central encoder pill and the colored embedding strips.
caption: CytoWave architecture and two-stage self-supervised pretraining. Stage 1: Learning control representations via masked gene expression and recovery using a joint Transformer encoder with FiLM-conditioned gene embeddings. Stage 2: Learning a genetic perturbation operator by jointly predicting cellular responses after perturbation (MSE loss) and contrastive perturbation alignment, where predicted perturbation embeddings are aligned with ground-truth masked perturbation embeddings with in-batch InfoNCE loss.
abstract: Predicting gene expression under perturbations from single-cell data is a fundamental task for modeling cellular responses, with applications in discovering gene function and designing therapeutics. However, existing methods often struggle to generalize across datasets due to differences in experimental protocols, biological contexts, and species. We present \textbf{CytoWave}, a perturbation-centric pretraining framework for single-cell genetic perturbation response prediction. We leverage large-scale cross-species perturbation datasets unified via orthology and train CytoWave in a two-stage manner. In the first stage, we learn reference control cell states via masked gene expression recovery on unperturbed cells. In the second stage, we pretrain the model to predict perturbed gene expression given control states and perturbation signals, together with a contrastive objective that aligns latent representations of perturbation responses with perturbation signals. We perform strict dataset-held-out evaluation across multiple condition combinations and case studies of pathway activity changes, demonstrating consistent and effective performance of CytoWave in predicting single-cell genetic perturbation responses.
